title: Error Budget Decision Workbench and Stakeholder Commitment Profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Create an operational "decision workbench" and a set of stakeholder commitment profiles that make error-budget-driven decisions explicit, auditable, and actionable across Dedicated, Hosted, and Private deployments. The workbench is a lightweight UI + policy spec that surfaces: remaining error budget, burn rate trends, linked SLI regression test results, active rollouts and canary windows, automatic suggestion of throttle/rollback actions, and a quick path to authorize mitigations by profile. Stakeholder commitment profiles codify who can approve what (e.g., Platform on-call, Product PM, Security) and the escalation chain based on customer impact and time-to-remediate thresholds.

Why now: We recently observed two cross-team incidents where error-budget exhaustion led to ad-hoc manual rollbacks and confusion over who owned the decision. This caused delayed mitigation and duplicated work across Platform and Product. Teams have called for clearer runbooks and a system to translate SLI signal into deterministic actions tied to org roles.

Scope: 1) Design a decision workbench page within Console that reads existing SLI/EBS telemetry and shows suggested actions ranked by severity and predicted customer impact. 2) Define 4 stakeholder commitment profiles (Platform Stability, Product Owner, Incident Response, Compliance Escalation) with approval authority and fallback policies. 3) Add a one-click action flow for canary throttle, model fallback, and alert escalations with audit logs and links to PRs/rollouts. 4) Ship a small pilot with two teams (Serving Runtime and Console) and measure decision latency, incidence of manual rollbacks, and stakeholder satisfaction.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement automatic enforcement of rollback actions without human approval (that will be a follow-up). We will not onboard all teams in the pilot — only two focused orgs to validate the flow.

Success metrics: shortening mean time-to-decision after a sustained SLI breach by 40%, reducing duplicate rollback work by 60% in pilot, and achieving >80% positive feedback from pilot stakeholders about clarity of ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Console page drafts (Figma) reviewed and signed off by Design and two pilot PMs
Policy schema for stakeholder commitment profiles published and stored in repo (YAML spec link in attachments)
Console shows live error-budget status + burn rate with at least three suggested mitigations and one-click action workflow in staging
Audit logs capture approval actor, timestamp, and action reason for each decision during pilot
Pilot run completed with decision-latency and duplicate-work metrics collected and a feedback survey returned by stakeholders
